content:
A fish table game is a shared shooting game: every shot costs a bet you set, and a fish pays a multiple of that bet if your shot takes it. As a beginner, learn three things first: the bet-per-shot control, how quickly a balance moves, and the load and redeem rules. Outcomes are decided by the game software, so plan a first session as entertainment with a fixed budget.

What you are looking at

Fish tables look busy the first time you open one. Almost everything on screen falls into five groups:

  • Your cannon. One seat at the edge of the table. You aim it, typically by tapping or dragging, and it fires where you point.
  • The bet control. Usually plus and minus buttons near the cannon. This number is what each shot costs. It is the most important control in the game.
  • Your balance. Shown beside the cannon. It drops with every shot and rises when a fish is credited to you.
  • The fish. Small ones are common and pay small multiples. Large ones and bosses are rare, pay more, and soak up many shots.
  • Other players. Their cannons sit at the other seats and their shots land on the same fish. You share the room, but each balance is separate.

Extras such as lock-on aiming, special weapons or bonus fish differ from one provider to the next, so learn them inside the game you pick. The format itself is covered in what a fish table game is, and the glossary defines the terms you will see.

What you control and what you do not

You choose the room, the bet per shot, the target, and when you leave. Those choices decide how long a balance lasts and how much of it is exposed at any moment.

You do not control whether a shot takes a fish. The software decides that, and the providers of the games on Casinova do not publish odds. Good aim keeps you from wasting shots on empty water. It does not turn a fish table into a game you can beat with practice, and anyone who tells you otherwise is guessing or selling something.

Your first session

  1. Write down two numbers. The balance at which you will submit a redeem (at least 3x your load) and the balance at which you will close the app.
  2. Open the lowest-stake room and set the bet per shot to the table minimum. Leave it there for the whole session.
  3. Spend the first few minutes watching. See how fast fish cross, how many shots a mid-size fish absorbs, and how quickly your balance moves at the minimum bet.
  4. Shoot fish you can finish. Small and mid-size fish that are well inside the table are better practice than a boss the whole room is firing at.
  5. Glance at the balance often. In a fish room it changes every second, and it is easy to lose track.
  6. Stop at one of your numbers. If you reach the redeem number, go back to the Casinova game page, use Check Balance, and submit the redeem. The redeem guide covers the review step.

Five beginner mistakes

  • Raising the bet to recover. A higher bet per shot empties a balance faster. It does not change your chances per shot.
  • Chasing a boss across the screen. Shots at a fish that swims off before it is taken are simply spent.
  • Holding the fire button down. Continuous fire at the minimum bet is still continuous spending. Pause between targets.
  • Making a large first load. A $500 first load needs a $1,500 balance before redeem opens. Learn the game on a threshold you can see.
  • Believing timing tips. Nobody outside the provider knows when a fish will pay. Our boss fish and timing guide explains why.

content:
A boss fish is the largest, highest-paying target on a fish table, and there is no reliable way to predict when one will appear or which shot will take it. Appearances and results are decided by the game software, and the providers of the games on Casinova publish no schedule or odds. What you can plan is how much of your balance a boss is allowed to cost and what you do once you reach the 3x redeem threshold.

What a boss fish is

In the fish table genre, a boss is an oversized target that carries a much higher multiplier than ordinary fish and absorbs far more shots. It usually crosses the table slowly, often with its own music or animation, and every player in the room tends to turn their cannon toward it. The player whose shot takes the boss is credited with the payout; shots from everyone else are spent.

Designs vary by provider. Some tables have one boss type, some have several, and some add special fish that trigger a bonus round or an area effect. We do not list names, multipliers or sizes here because providers change them and Casinova does not set them. If you are new to the format, start with what a fish table game is.

What "jackpot" means in these lobbies

Jackpot is a loose word. In slots it usually means a top prize or a progressive-style counter attached to a machine. In fish rooms it may mean a boss payout or a separate prize feature. In every case the rules, the amounts and the trigger belong to the provider's software. Casinova handles your account, loads and redeems; it does not run, schedule or adjust the games.

Why timing tips do not hold up

  • No schedule is published. None of the providers of the live games at Casinova publishes how often a boss appears or what it takes to land one. A number quoted elsewhere is somebody's guess.
  • Seeing a boss is not the same as taking it. Even if a boss appeared on a fixed clock, the outcome of each shot would still be decided by the software.
  • The room is shared. Several players are firing at the same boss. More cannons means it is resolved sooner, and only one player is credited.

What a boss actually costs

Think in shots. If your bet per shot were $0.10 and you fired 100 shots at a boss, you would have spent $10 whether or not it was credited to you. At $0.50 per shot the same 100 shots cost $50. Those bet sizes are only examples, since each room sets its own range, but the arithmetic is the same everywhere: shots multiplied by bet per shot is what the attempt costs.

That makes a boss the most expensive decision on the table, which is why it deserves a rule made in advance.

A boss budget you can keep

  1. Set a cap per boss. Decide what share of your starting balance one boss attempt may cost. A small fraction, such as a tenth, is a reasonable start. When it is spent, turn the cannon elsewhere.
  2. Do not raise the bet for a boss. Keep the bet per shot you chose for the session. Raising it changes the cost of every shot, not just the lucky one.
  3. Skip bosses that are leaving. A boss near the edge of the screen may swim off before anyone takes it, and those shots are gone.
  4. Prefer fish you can finish. Mid-size fish in open water cost fewer shots and are contested by fewer players.
  5. Stop at your floor. Pick the balance at which you close the app before you load, and keep to it.

How to win at fish table games turns these into a full session plan.

How the 3x and 8x redeem rules change the boss decision

At Casinova, redeem opens when your game balance reaches 3x the load and is capped at 8x the load in total. A $20 first-deposit load is matched 100%, so $40 goes into the game, redeem opens at $60, and the cap for that load is $160.

  • Below 3x: you cannot redeem yet, so the temptation is to chase a boss to get there quickly. A capped boss budget matters most here, because an uncapped chase is the usual way a balance reaches zero.
  • At or above 3x: you now have something a boss chase can take away. Use Check Balance on the Casinova game page and consider submitting a redeem before you fire another expensive volley. Submitting a redeem starts the review; the credits leave the game only after staff approve it. Several partial redeems against one load are allowed up to the 8x total, $5 to $500 per request, one at a time.
  • Near 8x: a redeem request cannot exceed what is left under the 8x cap for that load, so a balance already at that level gains no extra redeem room from a boss chase.
  • After a new load: the 3x threshold and the 8x cap are worked out from your most recent completed load, so a later, smaller load resets them.

Redeems need an approved government ID and are reviewed by staff, and we do not promise a payout time. The redeem guide explains the steps.

FAQ

Can you predict when a boss fish will appear?

No. The providers of the games on Casinova do not publish boss schedules, and the game software decides both when a boss appears and whether a shot takes it. Timers quoted online are not from the providers.

Is there a best time of day to hunt boss fish?

Nothing published supports one. A quieter room means fewer players firing at the same target, which gives you cleaner shots, but it does not change how the software resolves them.

Should I raise my bet when a boss shows up?

That is your call, but understand the cost. A higher bet per shot spends your balance faster, and only the player whose shot takes the boss is credited. Setting a fixed amount you are willing to spend per boss is the safer habit.

Does Casinova control boss fish or jackpots?

No. The games run on each provider's software. Casinova creates your game login, loads credits from your wallet and processes redeems under the 3x and 8x rules.

Casinova does not make or run Juwa. The provider runs the games and decides their results. Casinova creates your Juwa login, moves credits in and out of it, and reviews redeems.

What a fish room is like

If you have never played one, here is the format in the genre generally:

  • You pick a room. Rooms are usually grouped by stake, each with its own range for the bet per shot.
  • You sit at a cannon. Other players hold the other seats. Everyone shoots at the same fish, but each player has a separate balance.
  • You set a bet per shot. Every shot subtracts that amount. This setting decides how fast your balance moves more than anything else.
  • Fish carry multipliers. Small fish are common and pay little. Large fish and bosses pay more, take many shots and attract the whole table.
  • The table never stops. There are no rounds to wait for. You join, play and leave when you choose.

Many fish tables also include aids such as lock-on targeting or special weapons. Which of these Juwa offers, and what they are called, is set by the provider and can change, so learn them in the app. For the format in depth, read what a fish table game is.

Is Juwa a game of skill?

You make real decisions in a fish room: which room, what bet, which fish, how long to stay. They affect how long a balance lasts. Whether any single shot takes a fish is decided by the software. Nobody can time a boss or read a table, and the feature names and timers you may have seen quoted for Juwa are not published by the provider. Our boss fish and timing guide explains why those claims do not hold up.

The slots and table-style side

Juwa is not only fish. The slots work the usual way: pick a machine, set a bet, spin. The table-style games give a slower, more deliberate change of pace. Load a small amount, open the lowest-stake fish room and set the bet per shot to the minimum. Spend a few minutes watching how the fish move before you fire much. content:
No strategy makes a fish table pay, because each shot is resolved by the game software and no provider publishes odds. What you can control is your budget, your bet per shot, how long you play and when you redeem. At Casinova Gaming the redeem rules, 3x the load to open and 8x as the cap, should shape those decisions more than any aiming tip.

What you cannot control

  • Whether a shot takes a fish. The software decides. Two identical shots at the same fish can end differently.
  • When large fish or bosses appear. No schedule is published. See our boss fish and timing guide.
  • What other players do. The room is shared, and only the player whose shot takes a fish is credited.
  • The odds. They are not published by the providers of the games on Casinova, so no one can truthfully tell you one game or room pays better.

Any guide promising a method that "works" is ignoring this list. Everything below is about the parts that are in your hands.

What you can control

1. The budget

Decide what the session may cost before you deposit, and treat that as money spent on entertainment. Loads run from $5 to $500. A smaller load means a smaller threshold and less at risk.

2. The bet per shot

This is your real stake. Balance divided by bet per shot is how many shots you have if nothing is credited. The bet sizes below are examples only, since each room sets its own range.

BalanceExample bet per shotShots before any payout
$40$0.05800
$40$0.20200
$40$1.0040

The same balance is either a long session or a very short one. Start at the table minimum. If you raise the bet, do it because your balance has grown and you have chosen to, not because you are behind.

3. The targets

Aim does not change the software's decision, but it does stop you paying for shots that hit nothing. Fire at fish that are well inside the table, prefer small and mid-size fish you can finish, and stop firing between targets. Put a cap on what any single boss may cost you.

4. The room

Pick the lowest-stake room while you learn. A quieter room gives you cleaner shots because fewer cannons are aimed at each fish. It does not improve the odds.

5. The length of the session

Set a time limit as well as a money limit. Fish tables run continuously with no natural break, and tired players make expensive choices. When the time is up, stop, whatever the balance says.

Let the redeem rules set your targets

Redeem at Casinova opens when your game balance reaches 3x the load and is capped at 8x the load in total. Your first deposit is matched 100% at load and your second 50%, which moves your starting balance closer to the threshold.

LoadIn game, first deposit (100%)In game, second deposit (50%)Redeem opens (3x)Cap (8x)
$10$20$15$30$80
$20$40$30$60$160
$50$100$75$150$400
$100$200$150$300$800

Three decisions follow from these numbers:

  • Before you load, pick the load by the threshold. Ask whether 3x that amount is a balance you would be glad to stop at. If the answer is no, the load is too big for the session you have in mind.
  • At 3x, you have a real choice. You may submit a redeem for part of the balance, for all of it, or continue playing. Submitting a redeem starts the review; the credits leave the game only after staff approve it. Several partial redeems against one load are allowed up to the 8x total, $5 to $500 per request, one at a time.
  • Near 8x, stop. A redeem request cannot exceed what is left under the 8x cap for that load, so playing on with a balance at that level adds risk without adding redeem room.
  • A new load resets the numbers. The 3x threshold and the 8x cap are worked out from your most recent completed load, so a later, smaller load resets them.

Redeems need an approved government ID and are reviewed by staff, with no promised payout time, so upload your ID before you play. Use Check Balance in the game panel before you submit. The redeem guide and how payouts work explain the process, and the bonus guide covers the match.

A session plan you can copy

  1. Choose the load and write down three numbers: the redeem number (at least 3x the load), the stop number (the balance at which you quit) and a time limit.
  2. Load, open the lowest-stake room, set the minimum bet per shot.
  3. Play small and mid-size fish. Check the balance every few minutes.
  4. At the redeem number, go back to Casinova, tap Check Balance and submit a redeem for at least part of it.
  5. At the stop number or the time limit, close the app.

Advice to ignore

  • "Save high power for the boss." A higher bet costs more per shot for everyone, lucky or not.
  • "The table is due." Past shots do not change the next one.
  • "This room is hot." Nobody outside the provider can know that.
  • "Enter this code for a bonus." There are no promo codes at Casinova.

Where to play fish tables at Casinova

Five live games list fish games in their mix: Game Vault, Juwa, MR All In One, Vegas Sweeps and Gameroom. For Juwa in particular, playing Juwa well applies these ideas to that app, and first-timers should begin with the beginner first-session guide.

FAQ

Is there a strategy that reliably wins at fish table games?

No. Each shot is resolved by the game software and odds are not published, so no method produces reliable wins. Budgeting and a low bet per shot make a balance last longer; they do not change the outcome of a shot.

What bet per shot should I use?

Start at the minimum the room allows. Your balance divided by the bet per shot is the number of shots you can afford without a payout, so a lower bet gives you a longer session.

When should I redeem?

Redeem opens when your game balance reaches 3x the load. Submitting a redeem starts the review; the credits leave the game only after staff approve it, and an approved ID is required. You can make several partial redeems against one load, $5 to $500 each and one at a time, up to 8x the load in total.

Do fish tables pay better than slots?

No one can say, because neither format has published odds in these games. Fish tables ask for more decisions; slots ask for fewer. Pick the one you enjoy and keep to your limits.
